original_question: Let F be a holomorphic foliation on the unit polydisc Dk ⊂ Ck whose leaves have dimension d > 1 and are tangent to holomorphic (1,0)-forms α1, ..., α_{k-d} that satisfy the Frobenius condition ∂α_j = Σ_{l=1}^{k-d} α_l ∧ β_{j,l}. Can F always be approximated by foliations on Ck or Pk? More precisely, can the forms α_j be approximated uniformly on compact subsets of Dk by entire forms, or by polynomial forms, that still satisfy the same Frobenius condition?
target_in_paper: Problem 11.1 in Section 11, "Approximation of foliations with leaves of higher dimension."
correct_elements: The draft is already very close to the paper's actual target. It correctly identifies the local setting of a holomorphic foliation on the unit polydisc, the case of leaves of dimension greater than 1, the description by holomorphic 1-forms \(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{k-d}\), the Frobenius-type integrability condition involving forms \(\beta_{j,l}\), and the precise approximation question by entire forms or by polynomial forms with compact-open convergence on the polydisc while preserving integrability. This is essentially Problem 11.1.
missing_details: The paper requires the leaf dimension to satisfy \(1<d<k\), not only \(d>1\).
The defining forms \(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{k-d}\) are assumed to be linearly independent at a generic point of the unit polydisc.
The paper states the Frobenius condition using the exterior derivative \(d\alpha_j\), not \(\partial\alpha_j\), although for holomorphic 1-forms these agree in type.
The forms \(\beta_{j,l}\) are holomorphic 1-forms on the same unit polydisc.

To approximate the foliation by foliations, the approximating entire or polynomial forms should themselves define foliations, so they must still satisfy the Frobenius condition and remain generically linearly independent.
The paper explicitly records an equivalent formulation of the Frobenius condition: \(\alpha_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\alpha_{k-d}\wedge d\alpha_j=0\) for every \(j\).

The projective part should not be broadened beyond the paper: the paper's 'more precise' formulation is simply approximation by polynomial 1-forms, without adding extra projective homogeneity conditions.
refined_question: Let \(\mathcal F\) be a holomorphic foliation on the unit polydisc \(\mathbb D^k\subset \mathbb C^k\) whose leaves have dimension \(d\) with \(1<d<k\). Suppose that \(\mathcal F\) is tangent to holomorphic 1-forms \(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{k-d}\) on \(\mathbb D^k\) that are linearly independent at a generic point of \(\mathbb D^k\) and satisfy the Frobenius integrability condition \(d\alpha_j=\sum_{l=1}^{k-d}\alpha_l\wedge\beta_{j,l}\) for some holomorphic 1-forms \(\beta_{j,l}\) on \(\mathbb D^k\). Is it always possible to approximate \(\mathcal F\) by foliations in \(\mathbb C^k\) or \(\mathbb P^k\)? More precisely, can \(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{k-d}\) be approximated uniformly on compact subsets of \(\mathbb D^k\) by entire holomorphic 1-forms, respectively by polynomial 1-forms, that still satisfy the same Frobenius condition and hence define foliations of the same codimension?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent formulation stated in Section 11: under the same hypotheses, one may replace the condition \(d\alpha_j=\sum_{l=1}^{k-d}\alpha_l\wedge\beta_{j,l}\) by \(\alpha_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\alpha_{k-d}\wedge d\alpha_j=0\) for every \(1\le j\le k-d\), and ask the same compact-open approximation question by entire or polynomial 1-forms satisfying these wedge identities.
justification: The draft is targeting the paper's exact local approximation problem, namely Section 11, Problem 11.1, not a broader neighboring conjecture. The opening paragraph of Section 11 supplies the full setup: the unit polydisc, the range \(1<d<k\), the defining holomorphic 1-forms, their generic linear independence, and the Frobenius condition together with its equivalent wedge formulation. Problem 11.1 then asks precisely whether such a foliation can be approximated by foliations in \(\mathbb C^k\) or \(\mathbb P^k\), more precisely by entire forms or polynomial forms preserving the Frobenius condition. The sentence immediately after the problem mentions Bogomolov's Stein-manifold question only as motivation, so the refined question should stay narrowly with this local approximation problem rather than being broadened to the ambient embedding conjecture.
